gap.heading: Why it exists
gap.sub: Credentials verify the keys. They do not verify the person holding them. A stolen password, a compromised OTP, a phished login all produce sessions that look legitimate because the correct credentials were used. Behavioural Biometrics reads the one signal that cannot be transferred between people: how someone physically types, touches, swipes, and holds their device.
hero.heading: Continuous, passive, frictionless behavioural intelligence — across every session.
hero.sub: An SDK-based module that reads how a person physically interacts with their device during a session and converts that interaction into a behavioural identity: unique to the individual, continuously refined, and impossible to replicate at scale.

reader.heading: What It Does
reader.slides[0].body: Every person interacts with their device in a way that is measurably unique. This cluster reads the full physical layer of that interaction, passively, with no friction to the user.
reader.slides[0].cards[0].label: Typing rhythm
reader.slides[0].cards[1].label: Touch pressure
reader.slides[0].cards[2].label: Swipe curvature
reader.slides[0].cards[3].label: Handling posture
reader.slides[0].points:
Typing rhythm, speed, dwell time, and flight time between keystrokes
Touch pressure, contact area, and tap precision
Swipe velocity, direction, and curvature
Scroll cadence and acceleration
Gyroscope, accelerometer, and device orientation data
Device handling posture: one-handed, two-handed, stationary, or in motion
reader.slides[0].title: Typing and Touch Patterns
reader.slides[1].body: Beyond how someone types or taps, the flow of a session carries its own signal. How a person moves through a form, which fields they pause on, and how they input data reveals whether the session is genuine, rehearsed, or externally guided.
reader.slides[1].cards[0].label: Field sequence
reader.slides[1].cards[1].label: Form hesitation
reader.slides[1].cards[2].label: Copy-paste
reader.slides[1].cards[3].label: Session duration
reader.slides[1].points:
Navigation sequence and field-focus patterns
Form-filling speed and hesitation points
Copy-paste and autofill detection
Context switching and background activity
Session duration relative to task complexity
reader.slides[1].title: Navigation and Session Flow
reader.slides[2].body: A single session produces a snapshot. Multiple sessions produce an identity. This cluster builds a unique behavioural profile for each user and refines it with every interaction, so every future session is compared against the individual's own pattern, not a generic threshold.
reader.slides[2].cards[0].label: Baseline
reader.slides[2].cards[1].label: Sessions learned
reader.slides[2].cards[2].label: Deviation
reader.slides[2].cards[3].label: Cross-session
reader.slides[2].points:
Per-user baseline established from initial sessions
Continuously refined with each subsequent interaction
Baseline belongs to the individual account, not a population average
Cross-session consistency tracked over the account lifecycle
reader.slides[2].title: Behavioural Baseline
reader.slides[3].body: Human interaction carries natural variation. Automated interaction does not. This cluster identifies sessions driven by scripts, headless browsers, or programmatic input rather than a person.
reader.slides[3].cards[0].label: Timing variation
reader.slides[3].cards[1].label: Touch events
reader.slides[3].cards[2].label: Navigation
reader.slides[3].cards[3].label: Bot probability
reader.slides[3].points:
Uniform timing and absent touch variation flagged
Mechanical navigation sequences identified
Scripted form-filling patterns detected
Classified passively, with no challenge screen or interruption to genuine users
reader.slides[3].title: Bot and Automation Detection
reader.slides[4].body: In authorised-push-payment scams, the person on the device is real but is being guided through the transaction by a fraudster on the phone. The behaviour changes in ways that are invisible to credential checks but measurable in biometrics.
reader.slides[4].cards[0].label: Active call
reader.slides[4].cards[1].label: Input pattern
reader.slides[4].cards[2].label: Hesitation points
reader.slides[4].cards[3].label: Coaching likelihood
reader.slides[4].points:
Hesitation at unusual points in the session
Segmented, coached input patterns
Navigation pauses inconsistent with familiarity
Active call detection during the session
Indicators that the user is following verbal instruction rather than acting independently
reader.slides[4].title: Scam and Coercion Detection
reader.sub: One SDK, reading the session as it happens. Five clusters of behavioural intelligence.
